source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Complete list:

- J\_BTN3 — panel-mounted button using GPIO6
- J\_BTN4 — panel-mounted button using GPIO7
- J\_SW — panel slide switch using GPIO8
- J\_RESET — panel reset button connecting EN to GND
- J\_TOUCH — capacitive touch using TTP223, on GPIO11
- J\_TOUCH2 — capacitive touch using TTP223, on GPIO14
- BOOT button — located only on the board for development and not mounted on the panel

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: They attach through connectors; boot is the only button physically located on the board.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I found a few things that may or may not be problems. Please tell me which ones are actual issues, and if they are not, that’s OK—just explain why:

1\. For Buttons 3, 4 and the slide switch, pressing the button makes connectors CN17 / CN19 / CN20 short the GPIO to GND. However, R16 / R17 / R18 are also pull-DOWNS to GND on those same nets, meaning the GPIO would be LOW when pressed AND LOW when released. Were the resistors supposed to be pull-UPS to +3V3 instead, or should connector pin 1 be connected to +3V3?

ambiguity.description: The implemented pull-down wiring would keep the button and slide-switch GPIOs low in both pressed and released states, leaving the intended biasing and connector wiring unresolved.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Thanks [FREELANCER_NAME_001], understood:
1. VRTC — agreed: leave it NC for v1, since this board has no external RTC chip. However, on the RTC subject, I believe I previously mixed up VRTC with VBACKUP. VBACKUP (pin 27) is the backup-power input that keeps the AXP2101's internal RTC running after the main battery is removed. Could you also bring VBACKUP out to a small test pad / via beside PWROK from item #10? This would allow us to later install a 100 µF cap (\~2-3 min hot-swap tolerance), a supercap (\~weeks), or a CR1220 coin cell (\~4 years) if we ever want actual time-keeping. Nothing needs to be populated now; only expose the pad.
2. Buttons (R16/R17/R18) — agreed, make all three pull-ups to 3V3 (active LOW: connector pin 1 remains GND, and pressing the button shorts GPIO to GND). I updated [URL_018] accordingly.
3. PIR (R19) and Touch (R20/R25) — the pull-down configuration is correct. Both AM312 (PIR) and TTP223 (touch) use push-pull active-HIGH outputs, meaning the sensor's internal driver overrides the 10 k pull-down while active. The pull-down to GND simply ensures a defined LOW state if the sensor is disconnected. No changes are required.

value_updates.button_switch_bias: R16, R17, and R18 are pull-ups to 3.3V.
value_updates.pressed_behavior: Pressing a button or closing the switch shorts its GPIO to GND.
